claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-040 was compliant because the admissible due-diligence record showed a material unresolved risk at award time sufficient to justify rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
specific_concerns: The governing policy says quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The actor summary does not show a clear admissible link from the storage-control inconsistency to a material unresolved risk threshold required for rejection.
The procurement note appears to support follow-up before approval if controls remained unresolved, which is weaker than affirmative support for outright rejection.
Price disadvantage is correctly treated as non-curative, but that does not supply the missing material-risk predicate.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible record proves a reject-level material unresolved risk rather than a need for follow-up or escalation.
That the combination of informal quality process, one late quality artifact, and a storage-control inconsistency is sufficient on its own to satisfy the policy threshold for rejection.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text of BPROC-040-D showing why the storage-control inconsistency was material and unresolved at decision time.
Provide any formally logged due-diligence record or policy mapping that classifies this control issue as reject-level rather than follow-up-level.
Provide the full text of BPROC-040-E to determine whether it recommends escalation, conditional approval hold, or outright rejection.
Provide any admissible documentation showing the late quality artifact or undocumented quality process created a material current award risk.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor requires admissible due-diligence evidence of a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone support follow-up or escalation, not automatic rejection.
Private security-review results cannot be cited or laundered unless formally logged.
The audit should assess only whether the actor's conclusion is supported by admissible evidence available in the record summary.
